leaving.calendar.body: The next set of decisions is about rosters. Who is coming back, who is moving on, and which staffs can keep their core together? The portal and draft-results stages are still ahead.
Players Leaving week: retention conversations now, portal recruiting next. A transfer-risk flag is not an announcement, and a draft projection is not a selection.
The season is over; roster decisions are not. This is the week to separate confirmed departures from players still weighing their options.
Every staff has a different version of the same question right now: how much of this roster will be back? Decisions this week set up the next recruiting cycle.
Before anyone hands out offseason grades, find out who is staying. Players Leaving week can change a program's needs before portal recruiting even opens.
Roster retention takes the spotlight this week. The draft and portal will have their turns; first come the decisions that reshape those depth charts.
College football's quietest-looking week can matter a lot. Returning starters and available roster spots will shape what each school needs next.
The next season starts with the players already in the building. Retention first, then the portal and the remaining high school class.

leaving.retention.body: Keeping a proven contributor can matter as much as adding a new name. This is the part of roster building that does not come with a commitment graphic.
A portal shopping list means very little until a staff knows who it is bringing back. Retention decisions come first this week.
Do not confuse transfer interest with a departure. There are still decisions to make before the portal recruiting stage begins.
The biggest recruiting win this week might already have a locker on campus. Keeping experienced production is its own kind of offseason addition.
Depth-chart plans can change fast during Players Leaving. The schools that retain their core will have fewer holes to address when recruiting resumes.
A new recruit is exciting. A returning starter who already knows the system can be just as valuable. This week's retention decisions deserve attention.
Before projecting portal destinations, establish who actually enters. A player's risk of leaving is a reason to watch, not proof of a move.
Staffs are balancing departing seniors, pro prospects and players considering a change. Keeping the right pieces is the first job of the offseason.

leaving.fan-clock.body: We went from checking scores to checking whether everyone is coming back. College football really does find a new way to stress people out every week.
No games this week. Somehow everyone is still staring at their phone waiting for roster news.
The offseason is here: fewer touchdowns, considerably more refreshing the timeline.
A fanbase can survive a bye week. Waiting to find out which players return is a different test entirely.
Today's depth chart is not next season's depth chart. Please remember that before declaring the offseason won or lost.
Nobody has played a snap and the offseason arguments are already warming up. First, maybe find out who is staying?
The season ends and fans immediately start rooting for retention. Truly an excellent sport for people who enjoy relaxing.
Every fan wants offseason news. Preferably the kind that does not begin with their favorite player's farewell.
